purpose: Docket PR2: the durable workflow, fault tests and the simulated evaluation. Docket files incoming documents (leases, notices, invoices) against the right property record, and sends a document to a person when it is not sure. This PR runs each document as a Temporal workflow from upload to filed or reviewed, proves it survives crashes and retries, measures it on a held-out test set with simulated model answers, and keeps the simulation evidence in one committed archive.
mechanism:
1. docket/ingress.py and docket/api.py take an upload, store it idempotently and start one Temporal workflow per document (docket/workflows.py), run by docket/worker.py with activities in docket/activities.py (inputs and outputs typed in activities_schema.py; docket/runtime.py wires settings, storage and the model gateway).
2. The workflow steps: extract text (core/extraction.py), shortlist candidate records (core/candidates.py), let the model choose only among those candidates or none (docket/prompts.py, llm/gateway.py), score deterministically (core/scoring.py: continuous signal strengths, two independent signals for a strong match, a conflict always forces review, the auto-file threshold in config/scoring.json), then file idempotently or wait for a human review signal. Every document ends with one final ledger status and a reason.
3. Matching reads untrusted PDF text, so it has one input budget at the top of shortlist(): body up to 64,000 characters and 2,000 lines (after NFKC and casefold), subject up to 1,000, filename basename up to 255. A field over budget gets no fuzzy or address matching and the document goes to review with reason input_too_large; the explicit-ID scan still reads the full text. Shortlisting runs in a worker thread and batches its fuzzy comparisons.
4. docket/failpoints.py lets tests crash the worker at named points; tests/fault/ prove no double filing and a final status after restarts (verify.sh --fault).
5. The model gateway has export/import: export writes requests with no recording to evals/pending/, a stand-in model answers them into evals/answers/, import validates them and records them in evals/recordings/calls.jsonl with provenance {simulated_by, standing_in_for}. Live mode gives each document its own budget; daily and evaluation caps stay shared.
6. evals/pending/ and evals/answers/ are untracked working folders. docket/llm/archive.py and scripts/pack_exchange.py keep evals/recordings/exchange.jsonl.gz: each request and raw answer with SHA-256 hashes and provenance, packed deterministically and merged (never dropping a key); its --check runs in verify.sh. The secret scan (scripts/check_secrets.py) also reads the archive.
7. docket/evaluation.py runs the corpus (seed 7 tunes the threshold via scripts/tune_threshold.py; seed 11 is held out) and writes reports; scripts/reproduce_eval.py makes verify.sh fail unless the seed-11 report is a measured PASS that reproduces. `docket shadow-diff` compares the model's choice with the top rules candidate and defaults to the newest seed-11 report.
8. docket/cli.py exposes eval, shadow-diff and score; compose.yaml runs Postgres, Temporal, SeaweedFS (S3-compatible storage), the API and the worker on localhost only.
decisions:
- The model only chooses among real candidates or none; deterministic scoring decides filing. On the held-out seed the choose step changes no filing decision in v0.1, and the report says so.
- Two independent signals for strong, and any conflict goes to review: wrong filings cost more than reviews.
- Seed 7 tunes, seed 11 is held out; the rule for graded corpus variants was committed before seed 11 was measured.
- No API key: answers are simulated (Haiku, with Opus for the requests Haiku's safety filter falsely blocked), labelled in every report.
- Matching time is bounded by one input budget, not by per-pattern fixes; over budget goes to a person, never a silent cut, because a cut could hide a contradicting address.
- The simulation working folders are untracked; one deterministic archive is the evidence.
- SeaweedFS instead of MinIO, whose images could not be pulled.
- Rejected: a timeout around matching (Python cannot stop CPU-bound work in a thread); truncating long documents.
readers: README.md -> people trying or evaluating the project (recruiters, developers who clone it); docs/rerecord.md and evals/recordings/README.md -> people re-running the simulation or recording with a real key; docs/adr/ -> engineers who want the reasoning; code comments and docstrings -> the next maintainer. Cristian's rule for all of them: every comment, description and doc line deliberate, plain short sentences, terms defined on first use, no jargon-heavy decision prose.
